extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, interested parties, and clients seeking guidance on IP trials/appeals in Korea
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the Korean administrative and judicial procedures for appeals and trials concerning patents, utility models, trademarks, and designs, including who may bring each type of trial and the appellate paths (KIPT → Patent Court → Supreme Court).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex Parte vs Inter Parte distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: When a person has received a certain kind of examiner's decision on an application for patent, utility model, trademark, and design, that person may demand an appeal (Ex Parte). An IP rights holder or an interested person having a conflict with those IP rights may demand a trial (Inter Parte).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page distinguishes Ex Parte Cases (applicant or patentee challenging an examiner's action) from Inter Parte Cases (disputes between interested parties, patentees, or third parties). Examples and eligibility for each trial type are given in subsequent entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial against a Decision of Rejection (Final Rejection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trial against a Decision of Rejection (Final Rejection) is an Ex Parte case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May only be demanded by the applicant. If dissatisfied with a KIPT ruling on such a trial, the applicant must bring a suit naming the Commissioner of the KIPO as defendant in the Patent Court (see suits against KIPT rulings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial against a Decision of Revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Trial against a Decision of Revocation is listed as an Ex Parte case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May only be demanded by the Patentee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial for Correction (ex parte eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Trial for Correction appears under Ex Parte cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May only be demanded by the Patentee (per the page's statement about Ex Parte trials). Note: the page also lists 'Trial for Correction' among Inter Parte items; the explicit eligibility statement given is that a Trial for Correction may only be demanded by the Patentee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter Parte case types (listed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter Parte Cases include: Trial for Invalidation; Offensive Claim Scope Confirmation Trial; Defensive Claim Scope Confirmation Trial; Trial to Establish a Non-Exclusive License; Trial for Correction; Trial for Invalidation of Correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are trials between interested parties (or between an interested party and the patentee). Specific eligibility constraints for some of these types are described in other entries (e.g., who may demand invalidation or confirmation trials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial for Invalidation / Invalidation of registration / Invalidation of patent correction — eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A Trial for Invalidation, a Trial for Invalidation of the Registration of an Extension of Patent Right Duration, and a Trial for the Invalidation of a Patent Correction may only be demanded by an interested party or an examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page additionally states: 'any person may request an invalidation trial on the grounds that the patent falls under any of the subparagraphs of Article 133 of Korean patent Act (except sub paragraph(ii), registration provided the request is made after the and not more than establishment of the patent right date of the registration of the patent right.)' (verbatim language on timing in the source is garbled).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim scope confirmation trials — who may demand
rubrics_metrics.description: A Trial for Confirmation of the Scope of the Patent Right (offensive or defensive claim-scope confirmation) may be demanded by the Patentee or by an interested party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both 'offensive' (patentee seeks affirmation of scope against others) and 'defensive' (third party seeks confirmation re: alleged infringement) confirmation trials are listed under Inter Parte cases and share the same eligibility rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial to Establish a Non-Exclusive License — grounds for request
rubrics_metrics.description: When a later patentee is not able to work his/her patented invention without using the patent right of a prior patentee, or when the prior patentee refuses to grant permission to use the patent right without justifiable reasons, the later patentee may request a trial for the grant of a non-exclusive license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets the substantive criteria for entitlement to a non-exclusive license trial: inability to practice due to prior right and unjustified refusal to grant permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-instance procedure and role of KIPT, Patent Court, Supreme Court
rubrics_metrics.description: The trial system related to IP rights in Korea is a three instance procedure consisting of the Korean Intellectual Property Tribunal (KIPT), the Patent Court and the Supreme Court. The KIPT is the first instance for settlement of IP-related disputes and is independently operated within KIPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals brought against rulings of the trial board (KIPT) will come under the exclusive jurisdiction of the Patent Court; appeals against decisions of the Patent Court lie before the Korean Supreme Court. The Patent Court was established to reduce the former two-step administrative trial procedure to a single step and to secure independence and specialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive jurisdiction of Patent Court over suits against KIPT rulings
rubrics_metrics.description: Suits of dissatisfaction against any rulings of the KIPT and suits of dissatisfaction against a KIPT's Trial Examiner's Decision remain under the exclusive jurisdiction of the Patent Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies where judicial review of KIPT rulings is heard: Patent Court (equivalent status to High Courts in Korea's court structure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may bring suits against KIPT rulings / who may be defendants
rubrics_metrics.description: Suits of dissatisfaction against the rulings, etc. of the KIPT may be brought by the parties concerned, interveners, or parties whose intervention was rejected despite their petition for intervention in a parent trial or its re-trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a suit in the Patent Court the Commissioner of the KIPO is named as a defendant in principle. However, a suit against the ruling in an invalidation trial, a claim scope confirmation trial or a trial to establish a non-exclusive license requires that its counterpart (i.e., winner of the parent trial) be named as the defendant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Patent Court reversal and remand to KIPT
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent suit is held to be well-grounded, the Patent Court will reverse the ruling on the trial or the decision of rejection. Where the ruling on the trial or the decision of rejection is reversed by the suit in the Patent Court, the trial examiner of the KIPT will reexamine the case on remand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reasons constituting the basis for the reversal are binding upon the trial examiner with respect to the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to the Supreme Court — timeline and grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: A party dissatisfied with a judgment of the Patent Court may appeal finally to the Supreme Court within two (2) weeks from receipt of the original copy of judgment, on the grounds that the judgment appealed from is contrary to the law and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A demand for final appeal is to be submitted to the Patent Court instead of to the Supreme Court (procedural detail stated on the page).

rubrics_metrics.name: KIPT independent operation within KIPO
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPT (KIPT) is the first instance for settlement of IP-related disputes and is independently operated within the KIPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This indicates the administrative positioning of the tribunal (KIPT) as separate within the patent office rather than being an internal examiner-level decision only.
